newsitem.title: BERMUDA: Bermuda to swear in first woman premier.
newsitem.headline: Bermuda to swear in first woman premier.

text.p: Pamela Gordon, daughter of one of the fathers of modern Bermuda politics, was to be sworn in as the island's first woman premier, officials said on Tuesday.
Gordon, 41, now the environment minister, was the only member of the ruling United Bermuda Party nominated for premier by the Monday deadline, the UBP said. She will be sworn in on Thursday.
Gordon met with the party caucus early on Tuesday as Premier David Saul began clearing out his desk after stunning the British colony when he announced his resignation last week.

UBP sources said secret opinion polls conducted by the party revealed that Saul had failed to inspire voters and his decision to resign had to be made as soon as possible if the party was to stand any chance of defeating the opposition Progressive Labour Party in the next election, which must be held within 18 months.
Gordon, a member of parliament for less than four years, faced the daunting task of uniting a divided and dispirited party before the general election, political experts said.

Her father, Trinidad-born physician E.F. Gordon, was a founder of the Bermuda Industrial Union and a controversial member of parliament in the 1940s and 1950s who pressed the island's white power structure to give way to growing black political involvement.

Saul evoked anger within UBP ranks when he granted former Premier Sir John Swan permission to open McDonald's fast-food restaurants in this conservative colony. The dispute split the party just as wounds were healing over a 1995 referendum rejecting independence. Bermuda has been a British colony for more than 380 years..
Gordon was expected to announce her new cabinet next week.
